think.label: Think · the storeroom floor (produced: Claire)
think.title: A Missing Side
think.script: Welcome back to Leonardo's workshop in Milan. Last time, you counted gold. Today, something is missing. The storeroom floor is 7 feet wide. Bernardo counted 56 floor tiles. Each tile is a square, 1 foot on every side, and the tiles cover the whole floor with none left over. But crates block the far wall, so nobody can measure how long the room is. Look at the floor and the tiles. What do you notice? What do you wonder? Write it down. Then make a guess: is the floor longer than it is wide, or shorter? Hold on to your guess, and find out your own way.

learn.label: Lesson · the main video: find a missing side (produced: Claire + Leonardo)
learn.title: Find a Missing Side: Side × ? = Area
learn.where: Lesson tab, Learn it station, top

parts.label: The panel
parts.title: 5 in × ? = 65 sq in
parts.body: Build rows of 5, count the rows, divide, check.

learn.script:
[Leonardo] Come in, come in. Bernardo has 65 gold sheets for a new panel, and the panel must be 5 inches wide. How long will it be? A careful worker would know before cutting the wood. Would you? I'll watch.

Here is the panel. We know two things. The area is 65 square inches. One side is 5 inches. The other side is missing. In what units is each one given? The area is in square inches. The side is in inches. They match, so we can start.

Each gold sheet covers 1 square inch. One row across the panel takes 5 sheets. Watch. One row: 5. Another row: 10. Keep going, row after row, all the way to 65. Now every sheet is used.

How many rows did we make? Let's count. 13 rows. Each row is 1 inch of the length. So the panel is 13 inches long.

Here is what we were really asking: 5 times what number makes 65? That is a missing factor. And we find a missing factor by dividing. 65 divided by 5 is 13.

Now check by multiplying. 13 times 5 is 65. That is the area. It matches.

Watch the unit. The area is in square inches. But the missing side is a length, so it is 13 inches, not 13 square inches. And if the side you know is in feet, change it to inches first.

So, to find a missing side, ask: the side I know, times what, makes the area? Divide the area by the side you know. Then multiply to check.

[Leonardo] Thirteen inches. Bernardo can cut the wood now. But what if the side I knew were in feet? Your turn first. Try the panel below.

do.title: Let's Do Some Together

parts.label: Problem 2
parts.title: Area 84 sq in, one side ½ ft
parts.body: Find the other side in inches.

do.script: Let's do a few together. Problem 1. A floor covers 76 square feet, and it is 4 feet wide. How long is it? The area is in square feet, and the side is in feet. They match. So, 4 times what makes 76? I'll build rows of 4. Row after row, until all 76 tiles are used. Now count the rows. 19 rows. 76 divided by 4 is 19. Check: 19 times 4 is 76. The floor is 19 feet long. Problem 2. Your turn first. Pause the video and try this one. Then press play and check. The area is 84 square inches, and one side is one half of a foot. The units don't match. Half of 12 inches is 6 inches. So, 6 times what makes 84? 84 divided by 6 is 14. Check: 14 times 6 is 84. The side is 14 inches. Problem 3. Watch out for this one. A rectangle covers 48 square inches, and one side is 1 foot. Someone wrote 48 divided by 1 is 48 inches. But the units don't match. 1 foot is 12 inches. 48 divided by 12 is 4. The side is 4 inches. Same units first, then divide.

parts.label: The big question
parts.title: Area and one side?
parts.body: Side × ? = area. Divide, then multiply to check.

wrap.script: The storeroom floor is done. Every tile is in its place. So, if you know the area and one side, how can you find the other side? Ask: the side I know, times what, makes the area? Put both in the same units first. Divide the area by that side. Then multiply to check that you get the area back. Next time, the Duke wants a gold border around his mirror. A border isn't one plain rectangle. That's Area of Composite Figures. See you in the workshop.
